positions.text: Authority that exists when reasoning begins is insufficient if it can disappear before an effect becomes durable. He and Yu add a concrete commit-time mechanism to this authority-drift problem. Their strict profile holds registered data, evidence, policy, and authority premises through durability; their compatible profile recertifies the effect against current dependencies and policy. The extension is conditional on complete registered footprints, trusted mediation, and effects that cannot bypass the gate. It does not establish semantic truth or production-wide safety.

positions.text: Agreement is not an outcome measure. Shao's matched Wason-task replays show that language-model groups reached consensus more often than human groups while simulated consensus failed to track collective accuracy. This result supports evaluation grounded in observed outcomes under stated conditions: a consensus signal can reflect correlated error and cannot independently establish correctness. The finding does not test reputation-weighted governance. It is limited to one objective reasoning task, one principal served build, an exploratory cross-family point, and remaining endpoint-measurement asymmetries.
